definition: HPO Speedup Techniques reduce the cost or wall-clock time of hyperparameter search. The lecture material emphasizes early stopping, multi-fidelity evaluation, learning-curve information, parallelism, and reuse of information from previous trials.
intuition: Make each search decision cheaper or make bad trials stop sooner; the goal is better performance per unit of compute, not just more trials.
advantages: Combines early stopping, fidelity reduction, parallelism, and information reuse.
Improves quality found per unit of time or compute.
limitations: Parallel and asynchronous search may consume budget less efficiently than carefully sequenced trials.
Speedups can reduce fidelity or introduce ranking bias.
